skill.name: qiaomu-campus-resume
skill.description: Creates ATS-friendly campus resumes from interviews, existing resumes, or job descriptions. Produces validated HTML and PDF layouts without inventing candidate facts.
skill.summary: Build evidence-based resumes for students, graduates, and internship applicants.
skill.author: joeseesun

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from documentation, Chinese text, catalog URLs, and fixed local tool invocations. One medium-risk DOCX decompression issue remains because archive expansion is not bounded.

remediation.issue: DOCX parsing does not limit the uncompressed size or compression ratio of word/document.xml.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect ZipInfo before reading, reject oversized or highly compressed members, and stream with a strict decompressed-byte limit.

content.value_statement: Students often struggle to turn scattered experience into credible, role-focused resumes. This skill interviews candidates, maps evidence to job requirements, and generates validated HTML and PDF files.
actual_capabilities: Interviews candidates one question at a time and records confirmed facts in a local evidence ledger.
Extracts text from local PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown, and CSV resume files.
Maps job requirements to supported evidence, gaps, and resume sections.
Validates contact details, timelines, evidence links, content structure, and unsupported placeholders.
Generates single-column HTML and PDF resumes across six ATS-friendly themes.
Checks PDF page size, page count, text extraction, encryption status, and embedded fonts when local tools are available.
limitations: It cannot verify that candidate statements are true beyond provided evidence and explicit confirmation.
It does not support academic CVs, executive resumes, portfolio websites, cover letters, or automated job applications.
PDF generation requires a compatible local browser and selected themes may require licensed local fonts.
Scanned resumes need separate local OCR with user consent.

use_cases.title: Create a first resume
use_cases.description: Turn projects, coursework, internships, and campus activities into a focused resume through a guided interview.

use_cases.title: Tailor an application
use_cases.description: Compare an existing resume with a job description and rewrite only claims supported by candidate evidence.

use_cases.title: Improve resume presentation
use_cases.description: Preserve confirmed content while producing a cleaner single-column layout and validated PDF output.

prompt_templates.title: Start my first resume
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me for a [target role] resume. Ask one question at a time. Use only facts I confirm.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner creation from no existing resume

prompt_templates.title: Reformat my resume
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract facts from my attached resume. Keep the wording and facts unchanged. Create a clean one-page [theme] PDF.

prompt_templates.title: Tailor to a job description
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my resume with this [job description]. Show requirements, supporting evidence, and gaps. Then tailor the resume without inventing skills or results.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and compare themes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the confirmed resume data to generate all six themes. Validate each PDF, compare readability, and recommend the best version for [target role].

output_examples.input: I need a backend internship resume and have two course projects but no previous resume.
output_examples.output: A guided evidence interview, a confirmed fact summary, and a one-page technical resume with editable HTML and validated PDF files.

output_examples.input: Tailor my current resume to this data analyst job description without adding unsupported keywords.
output: A requirements-to-evidence comparison that identifies supported strengths and honest gaps.
A revised resume that prioritizes relevant projects, tools, and measurable results already confirmed by the candidate.
A validation report covering content structure and PDF checks.

output_examples.input: Keep my resume content unchanged and show several professional layouts.
output_examples.output: Six single-column resume versions using the same confirmed facts, plus a comparison manifest and validation results.

best_practices: Provide the target role, current resume, and job description when available.
Confirm every fact summary and explain whether each result represents personal or team work.
Review the final PDF visually and test every contact link before applying.
anti_patterns: Do not request invented metrics, employers, responsibilities, tools, or awards.
Do not treat job description keywords as candidate skills without supporting evidence.
Do not upload private identity numbers, passwords, tokens, full addresses, or unrelated personal records.

faq.question: Can it create a resume when I have no draft?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks one focused question at a time and builds a resume after facts and evidence are confirmed.

faq.question: Can it tailor a resume to a job description?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps each requirement to evidence or a gap, then uses only supported claims.

faq.question: Will it invent achievements or numbers?
faq.answer: No. The workflow requires evidence and candidate confirmation before final generation.

faq.question: Which input formats are supported?
faq.answer: The local extractor supports PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown, and CSV files. Scanned documents require separate OCR.

faq.question: What files does it produce?
faq.answer: It can produce editable HTML, a text-based PDF, resume data, an evidence ledger, and validation results.

faq.question: Does it guarantee interviews or an ATS score?
faq.answer: No. It validates structure and files but cannot predict recruiter decisions or platform-specific scores.
